newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow drop depresses Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow drop depresses Australian stocks at open.

text.p: Australian shares slid at the open on Tuesday as trading resumed after the holiday long weekend, with the Dow's fourth consecutive losing day casting a weaker pall over the local market.
From opening, the All Ordinaries index lost 16.5 points to 2,406.5.
With the market closed on Monday for the Australia Day holiday, brokers said the early weakness was no surprise as two days of Dow losses had to be absorbed by the local bourse.
"It's down on back of the U.S. It is much what you would have expected given the Dow has lost about 100 points in the last two days," said a Sydney-based dealer.
Losses were broadly spread, golds the main exception with the firmer bullion price providing a pick-me-up to the embattled sector.
Acacia Resources, adding three percent to A$2.20 (US$1.70), Newcrest, gaining 1.6 percent to A$5.13 and Normandy Mining whose scrip added 2.5 percent to A$1.63 were the pick of the bunch.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about five to three, while about 36 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
